title: Service-Normalized Hydrogen System Study
research_question: Under which combinations of hydrogen production, electricity, storage, transport, end-use conversion, and policy does hydrogen deliver additional climate, reliability, industrial, or energy-access value compared with direct electrification and competing fuels?

stages.name: demand_and_boundary_audit
stages.purpose: Construct hourly service ledger and separate energy, feedstock, emergency, and routine uses.

stages.name: pathway_and_lifecycle_characterization
stages.purpose: Parameterize energy, water, emissions, methane, capture, replacement, leakage, safety, and material burdens.

stages.name: service_level_process_comparison
stages.purpose: Compare hydrogen and alternatives at matched industrial, transport, chemical, and storage services.

stages.name: hub_infrastructure_and_grid_simulation
stages.purpose: Link production, electricity, storage, transport, offtake, and sector coupling under hourly constraints.

stages.name: stress_safety_and_demand_uncertainty
stages.purpose: Test correlated weather, outage, water, leakage, safety, supply-chain, and demand scenarios.

stages.name: out_of_sample_validation_and_adoption
stages.purpose: Validate held-out conditions and test investment, contracts, certification, and policy withdrawal.

safeguards: include methane, leakage, water, land, materials, and replacement
review hydrogen, ammonia, storage, pipeline, transport, and industrial safety
do not use announced projects as operating evidence
do not represent modeled results as observed facts
